data.did_you_know: Spring was considered to be a season of courtship and romance; perhaps the gentleman on the bridge in the red cap is trying to catch the attention of the lady next to him.
data.description: In this springtime scene, two fishermen wade in a river, dragging a net suspended between two poles. A noble couple on a bridge gestures toward other fishermen, who occupy the other side of this scene in other extant examples of this tapestry with a larger picture plane. In the background, townspeople walk on bridges that lead to the gateway of a town with brick walls and portals. In the far distance, farmers till the soil to sow new seeds, another typical activity associated with spring. The trees on the hills are just beginning to sprout new buds.

data.conservation_statement: This tapestry was woven with a wool warp and silk- and metal-thread weft. As can be seen in the photomicrograph at 40 times magnification, the core of the metal thread is yellow silk. Wound around the core like a barber pole is a narrow strip of metal that when analyzed was found to be a blend of silver and gold in a ratio of about 4.5 to 1. There is also a trace amount of copper used.
